h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֵׁנִי, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni — Maamar Bais

p: in order to equalize the years of the moon
with the years of the sun,
so that the season of Nissan should fall in Nissan
The reason the Torah insisted on equalizing them
"And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun,
and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold,
like the light of the seven days."
through the words of Torah (Bereishis Rabbah 1:1),
and on the first day it is written, "Let there be light,"
and "light" is written five times in it,
corresponding to the five Chumashim of the Torah
And when the luminaries were hung in place,
they were from the primordial light,
was the primordial light hidden away on Motza'ei Shabbos
and it was stored away for the tzaddikim for the future to come.
This is what it says, "like the light of the seven days,"
for throughout all seven days of Creation
מִשְׁתַּוִּים שְׁנוֹת הַלְּבָנָה עִם שְׁנוֹת הַחַמָּה
the years of the moon become equal with the years of the sun;
that is, then is the time to merit
that the light of the moon be like the light of the sun,
and the light of the sun be sevenfold,
like the light of the seven days.
And it is hinted in the verse (Tehillim 128:5),
and may you see the good of Yerushalayim":
the letters of "BeTuv" have the numerical value of nineteen,
to hint that every nineteen years
there is a preparation to merit the light that "was good,"
so that the light of the moon be like the light of the sun.
when seven leap months are made,
the years of the moon are equalized
with the years of the sun approximately,
and this is called a cycle,
(הִלְכוֹת קִדּוּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ פֶּרֶק ו הֲלָכָה י).
And this is why it is Adar that is doubled:
to be a preparation for being redeemed in Nissan.
The month of Adar was formed with the letter Kuf,
as it says in Sefer Yetzirah.
And it is found in the Arizal,
in his commentary on Sefer Yetzirah:
and it goes through the channel from Binah to Chesed,
and it was given to Naftali,
and He created, etc." End quote.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאוֹת קוֹף קָדוֹשׁ [שַׁבָּת קד, א],
That is, the letter Kuf stands for "kadosh" (Shabbos 104a),
to repair the blemish of the serpent;
and the month is designated for the eradication of Amalek,
who is the root of the evil inclination,
and through this it is a preparation
As for the order by which holiness enters the heart of Yisrael,
he said, "it goes through the channel from Binah to Chesed."
"and his heart will understand, and he will return";
and Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for the attribute of Gevurah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
and afterwards one merits the light:
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham"
and full with the blessing of Hashem, etc."
"What is meant by 'and full with the blessing of Hashem,
possess the west and the south'?
If you walk in My statutes,
you will inherit the World to Come,
which is likened to the sea, etc.
And why is it written 'yerashah,' etc.?
אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּכְּלָל
Rather, even the Holy One, blessed be He, is included,
וְעוֹד אָמְרוּ אֵין יָם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
And they further said: 'Sea' means nothing other than Torah,
If so, the secret of the verse will be:
Naftali is sated with the Favor
that fills the blessing of Hashem,
And he concluded, "and the wise will understand";
That is, this month is designated
for meriting the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
and as we have already said,
the letters are numbered and counted.
And in this month "they accepted it anew"
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה הַכְּפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית
for which the mountain had been held over them like a barrel,
And through the Torah she'b'al peh
to repair the blemish of the serpent from its root.
that shines forth upon Knesses Yisrael,
for the Hei is the Dalet of the Name Havayah,
and the closed Mem is the Upper World, Binah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רלו, ב)
which hints that the holiness will remain forever.
"Yam" has the numerical value of fifty,
for the baal teshuvah merits the fiftieth gate,
which is the place where baalei teshuvah stand
as we have said several times.
"And south" is the attribute of Chesed, as is known.
one merits the holiness of this Name,
for supernal Chesed issues from Chochmah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב),
Yud is Chochmah, and Hei is Binah.
that laughter should be in holiness
which is when one merits to be
sated with the favor of Hashem Yisbarach,
and that is when it shines from the root,
from the Aleph, the supernal Wonder.
"Then our mouth will be filled with laughter."
This is the root of the holiness of the month of Adar:
that one merits the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is from the dew of Atika,
that was stored away for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh,
to repair the blemish of the serpent,
and it is a preparation for being redeemed in Nissan.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 13b — “Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said: Acherim are speaking about the Nisan season, for it is written, Guard the month of spring: guard the spring season so that it falls within the month of Nisan.” The surrounding discussion gives differing thresholds for intercalation. Rav Tzadok uses its basic requirement that the lunar month and solar spring remain aligned.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 1:1 — “The Torah says: I was the instrument of the Holy One, blessed be He, in His craft. Ordinarily a human king who builds a palace does not build it by his own knowledge but by the knowledge of an architect. The architect does not build it by his own knowledge, but has plans and tablets to know how to make rooms and small doors. So the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into Torah and created the world.” Torah as the plan of Creation is the premise for Rav Tzadok's identification of primordial light with the Torah's light.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 12 — “In the future, when all of Torah she'b'al peh is complete … ‘and the light of the sun sevenfold, like the light of the seven days’: the light of the first Tablets.” Rav Tzadok reads Yeshayah's verse as a statement about Torah. The equalizing of moon and sun is the Oral Torah reaching the standing of the Written Torah.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 12:6 — “Rabbi Levi said in Rabbi Nezira's name: That light served for thirty-six hours: twelve on Friday, twelve on Shabbos night, and twelve on Shabbos day. When Adam sinned, God wished to hide it, but honored Shabbos. ... When the sun set at the departure of Shabbos, darkness began to serve, and Adam became afraid.” The Midrash distinguishes the light's thirty-six hours of service for Adam from the first-day light's original creation. Rav Tzadok relates the verse's light of seven days to the primordial light throughout Creation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis 2 — “The lights were diminished and separated, the light of the moon … the Written Torah; and through the holiness of Shabbos they become included in one another as in the future.” What the nineteen-year cycle prepares for, Shabbos already grants for a time. Each week it gives a foretaste of the moon's light equaling the sun's.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Kiddush HaChodesh 6:10 — “Every nineteen-year period containing seven intercalated years and twelve ordinary years is called a cycle. Why do we rely on this count? When you collect the days, hours, and parts of twelve ordinary years and seven intercalated years ... the total comes to nineteen solar years of 365 days and six hours each, with a remaining difference of only one hour and 485 parts in nineteen years.” The Rambam describes an approximation, explicitly retaining the small remainder. Rav Tzadok's spiritual interpretation of the nineteen-year cycle should not be read as mathematical identity between lunar and solar time.

paragraphs.text: Maamar Kedishin, attributed to the Arizal, on the letter Kuf — “Kuf: on the right hand, the thumb, outer joint; it goes through the channel from Binah to Chesed, is given to Naftali, and reigns over laughter; it created Pisces in the world, Adar in the year, and the spleen in the soul.” The Gra cites this work by name in his commentary on Sefer Yetzirah (1:1, “see Maamar Kedishin of the Arizal”) and reports its order in 5:3: “in the writings of the Arizal he wrote laughter for Naftali ... so that the tribes come in the order of the banners.” Rav Tzadok calls the work the Arizal's commentary on Sefer Yetzirah. His quotation follows its Kuf entry word for word.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 175b, Terumah — “Rabbi Shimon said: I see that wisdom includes everything. Supernal lovingkindness issues from wisdom; might, which is powerful judgment, issues from understanding. Yaakov completes the two sides. The patriarchs include everything, and Yaakov includes the patriarchs.” The original expressly gives the two derivations used here: chesed from chochmah and gevurah from binah. Rav Tzadok applies them to the flow through Yitzchak's attribute and then to Avraham's light and lovingkindness. The later repetition in this maamar is covered by this same original passage.

paragraphs.text: Ramban, Devarim 33:23, citing Sefer HaBahir — “In the Midrash of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah they said: Moshe said, If you walk in My statutes, you will inherit the World to Come, which is compared to the sea ... and this world, compared to the south. Why does Scripture say yerashah rather than yerash? Because even the Holy One, blessed be He, is included: rash Yah, inherit God. ... Everything is given to you; would that you keep His ways. They also said: Sea means none other than Torah, as it is said, Broader than the sea.” Ramban gives the plain meaning before the Bahir's interpretation. Rav Tzadok draws on the mystical inheritance of sea and south as Torah and the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 236b, Pinchas — “Rabbi Shimon opened: 'Hear, Israel, Hashem our God, Hashem is One.' The ayin is large, and so is the dalet; together they signify ed, witness. ... The letters shin-mem remain, with an open mem. Why is it not closed? Because the closed mem is the upper King—the alternate reading says 'upper world'; the open mem is the lower King—the alternate reading says 'lower world.'” The original expressly preserves 'world' as an alternate reading alongside 'King.' Rav Tzadok follows that reading when interpreting the closed mem through the upper world, binah. This is a textual variant, rather than a substitution of a general teaching about the sefiros.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 1 — “The gates of prayer are sometimes open, sometimes locked… but the sea is always open … and they merit the fiftieth gate, Binah, which is the World to Come.” The Midrash's image of the sea supports Rav Tzadok's link between “yam,” numerically fifty, and the gate of fifty. Like the sea, that gate is never closed to the baal teshuvah.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 34b — “Rabbi Abahu said: The place where penitents stand cannot be occupied by wholly righteous people, as it is said, Peace, peace to the far and to the near: first to the far, and afterward to the near.” Rabbi Abahu and Rabbi Yochanan interpret the verse differently. Rav Tzadok follows Rabbi Abahu's elevation of repentance in this passage.
